sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

literature_notes: All eight ledger lines (L1–L8) describe a single construct: full-length MAS1 (MasR / MAS1R) fused to YFP at its carboxy-terminus. The topology landmarks place the C-terminus (residues 284–325) firmly in the intracellular compartment. The tag therefore sits on the cytoplasmic face and cannot serve as an extracellular surface tag. L7 confirms the tagged receptor retains wild-type Ang-(1-7) binding affinity, and L2/L8 confirm plasma-membrane trafficking, but neither changes the topology of the tag itself. No ledger line supports any insertion at the extracellular N-terminus (residues 1–36), ECL1 (90–105), ECL2 (171–185), or ECL3 (251–262). Because the rules forbid proposing sites not grounded in the ledger, zero extracellular surface sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: YFP fused to the carboxy-terminus of full-length MasR; topology landmarks place residues 284–325 in the intracellular C-terminal tail, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface. Function preserved (same Ang-(1-7) affinity, L7) and receptor traffics to plasma membrane (L2, L8), making this a valid intracellular C-terminal label but not an extracellular surface tag.
